findings.rationale: In domain_kernel_source, when a command's decision emits an event that is the request event of an effect, the effect status map is advanced to Pending and its attempt counter is set to 1. The emitted-event guard only checks status != Pending and status != Succeeded; it omits Failed and TimedOut. After a failed/timed-out attempt, the retry action requires status == Failed || TimedOut to move status back to Pending, so a new emit on the same correlation is blocked by the Pending check. This creates a window where a stale Failed/TimedOut status is overwritten back to Pending, causing a repeated/inconsistent status transition.

evolve_assignments derives the assignment target root by taking the first alphanumeric/underscore token of the rendered target and mapping it via Context::state_name. This is an unstable scope key: when a target identifier collides with the root token of a different state field (e.g. a field name that is a prefix or shares the same lowered root), assignments to distinct state fields can collapse onto the same generated state identifier, producing an incorrect or repeated effect on state.

saga_condition replaces event name identifiers in an expression with the generated event flag via substring token replacement. Events are sorted by descending length, but the replacement is a bare identifier swap that can also match the event name when it is a sub-token inside a longer identifier, yielding an unstable token substitution and incorrect saga guard conditions.
